title: Tom Yum
subtitle: Thai hot and sour prawn soup with lemongrass and kaffir lime
excerpt: Thailand's most famous soup: a clear, fiery, intensely fragrant broth of lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce, with prawns and mushrooms, balanced with lime juice and a little palm sugar. Hot, sour, salty, and herbaceous.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tom yum (boiled sour) is Thailand's national soup and one of the most internationally recognised Thai dishes. Tom yum goong (with prawns) and tom yum gai (with chicken) are the two most common versions. The soup has a clear broth version (tom yum nam sai) and a creamy coconut milk version (tom yum nam khon); the clear version is the more traditional. The aromatic foundation of lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves is non-negotiable and defines the soup; fish sauce and lime juice provide the salt and sour. Tom yum paste (a ready-made version containing the aromatics and chilli) is widely used in Thailand and provides a shortcut at the cost of some freshness. The clear, non-coconut version is presented here.

content.text: The aromatics (lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves) are left whole and removed before eating: they flavour the broth but are too fibrous and intense to eat. Bruise the lemongrass and galangal well before adding to help them release more flavour. Do not boil the prawns hard; add them at the very end and remove the soup from the heat as soon as they are pink, about 2 minutes.

items.preparation: peeled and deveined; shells reserved if available
stalks, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
whole dried Thai bird's eye chillies; or 2 fresh red chillies, bruised

content.text: Bring the stock to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and chillies. Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse. Add the mushrooms and simmer for 3 minutes.

Add the prawns and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until just pink. Remove from the heat. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar. Taste: the soup should be a clear balance of hot, sour, salty, and slightly sweet. Adjust the fish sauce for salt, lime for sour.
Ladle into bowls, discarding the lemongrass, galangal, and whole chillies if preferred (or leave for authenticity and warn guests not to eat them). Garnish with fresh coriander and spring onion.
